subject: Dedicated capacity: compute safety net & SKU plan for Helion Health (long-context)
messages:

Cc: procurement@helionhealth.ai

Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing request — Helion long-context workloads

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the intro last week. We ran the initial production traces over the weekend and attached the query profile plus a short csv with P99 token lengths and sampling settings (see Helion_QueryProfile_v2.pdf, POC_metrics.csv). High-level summary: most requests are short (<=256 tokens) for embeddings and live routing, but the consent and chart-summarization flows produce long outputs (6k-20k tokens) for nightly batch jobs and for a small subset of real-time clinician assist sessions (low single-digit % of traffic).

Two asks from our side: 1) a recommended Dedicated SKU mix for a 12–24 month reserved commitment that covers steady traffic and peak bursts, and 2) an ops-level fallback plan if memory pressure hits during those long-context sessions. Cost sensitivity is material (we have internal budget targets) but we cannot compromise P99 latency for clinician-facing flows.

Can your team propose a safety-net plan (SKU mix + buffer + short list of operational mitigations)? Also looping in Procurement for contract/term questions.

Thanks,
Samantha Brooks
CTO, Helion Health
Samantha.Brooks@helionhealth.ai

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing request — Helion long-context workloads

Samantha — appreciate the profile and the detail. Quick read-through below with an initial sketch. Attaching a lightweight SKU matrix for the pilot (initial-sku-matrix.xlsx).

Topline recommendation (short): hybrid pool with explicit long-context headroom. Proposed committed mix (starting point):
- L4 instances: 55–65% of baseline slots — for embeddings, low-latency chat, and high-concurrency short requests
- A100 (40GB): 25–35% — for memory-heavy batched summary jobs and medium-length generations where fp16/amp helps throughput
- H100 (80GB/80GBx2 options): 10–15% — reserved specifically for the 6k–20k token sessions and RL/LLM-compute hotspots that need larger KV caches

Why this split? L4 offers best tokens-per-dollar for short requests and fast cold-start; A100 is the economic middle for many mixed workloads; H100 is expensive but provides the memory and kernel throughput for sustained long-context jobs. Key tradeoffs and operational mitigations:

- Memory pressure: for long-context interactive sessions we recommend session-aware slotting (pinning those sessions to H100 nodes) and proactive KV cache eviction policies.
- Predictable bursts: maintain a 20–30% burst buffer (composed of on-demand A100/H100 slots depending on region pricing) + automated fallback to quantized A100 variants if H100 slots are exhausted.
- Cost controls: continuous instrumentation of tokens-per-dollar by model/route; we can auto-scale L4 aggressively and cap H100/Reserve concurrency to preserve budget.

Next steps I'd propose:
1) short pilot (4 weeks): 2 H100 slots, 6 A100 slots, 18 L4 slots mapped to your query mix + synthetic load to validate P99.
2) production canary with 10% traffic for clinician flows behind circuit-breaker.
3) pricing/term sketch to lock reserve discount + burst pool (we have standard 24-month and 12-month options).

Would love Kimberly and Dev to add runbook/ops notes — copying them in. Happy to jump on a quick call tomorrow to walk this through.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Sr. Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing request — Helion long-context workloads

Thanks Jonas — adding a few ops-level constraints and mitigations so Procurement and your SREs have concrete items.

Operational guardrails:
- Quantization & model variants: suggest an A/B on int8-quantized A100 variants for batch summaries; if quality regresses we fallback to fp16 on A100.
- KV cache policies: keep session KV pinned on H100 for active clinician sessions; implement time-based TTL (e.g., 15m) and an LRU eviction for cold sessions.
- Continuous batching: enable continuous batching on L4 pool to maximize throughput for short requests; set a per-route latency SLO to avoid head-of-line blocking.
- Canary & rollback: canary rollout for any model or infra change (5% -> 25% -> 100%) with automatic rollback on P99 degradation > 15%.
- Fallback plumbing: if H100 capacity saturates, automatically: 1) throttle non-clinician long jobs (batch queue with retry), 2) redirect live clinician sessions to an A100-quantized fast path (with explicit consent/notification).

Capacity sizing note: the 20–30% burst buffer should be a mix of reserved-on-demand slots (A100) and a small H100 pool only for the highest-value sessions. We recommend a 1.25x slot headroom multiplier on the projected 95th percentile concurrent long-context sessions for safety.

Happy to draft a short runbook for your SREs that maps these to our console toggles.

—Kimberly Park
Director, Dedicated Ops, Redwood Inference

Samantha — appreciate the questions. Consolidating the ask into a short Mutual Action Plan and an operational safety-net we can sign to move forward. Attached a term sketch (commit-term-draft.pdf) but key points inline:

Proposed commitment & fallback plan (summary):
- Commit window: 24 months recommended (12-mo shown as alternative): 24-mo yields ~18–22% reserved discount across SKUs; 12-mo 10–12% discount. Exact number dependent on final slot counts/regions — finance will produce the quote.
- Recommended committed pool (example): H100: 10% of committed slots, A100: 30%, L4: 60% (adjustable quarterly).
- Safety buffer: keep 25% unallocated burst capacity (mix of on-demand A100 + 1–2 hot H100 nodes) to handle unpredicted long-context spikes.
- SLA: P99 latency objective for clinician routes — Redwood proposes a credit band tied to P99 miss rate for routes labeled "clinician-assist". We'll surface a formal SLA appendix for legal review; SOC2 Type II evidence and weekly audit-log export are standard for Dedicated/Private customers and we'll share the SOC2 package plus an export endpoint.
- Canary & rollouts: 5% -> 20% -> 100% with automated rollback thresholds as Kimberly outlined.

Operational timeline & milestones:
1) Week 0–2: pilot infra provisioning + small synthetic load test (validate P99 for clinician flow).
2) Week 3: pilot run with live traffic shadowing; adjust slot ratios and headroom.
3) Week 4: production canary (10% traffic) then ramp to target over two weeks.

Please let us know if the proposed H100 floor (10%) is acceptable; we can model two alternatives (H100 floor at 6% vs 12%) and show cost/latency deltas. If Procurement wants the detailed 12-mo/24-mo financial delta we can have our finance ops deliver a line-item quote by Monday.

Would you like a short call Monday to finalize the MAP and pricing path?

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Sr. Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
